title: PBIS Cafeteria Expectations Program
source_title: Bogan Weekly News | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content: Positive Behavioral Interventions and Supports (PBIS) We are so excited to continue the PBIS work we started last year! This week, we held Welcome Back assemblies with our second-fifth grade students. We have a lot of FUN opportunities planned for students this year:Bogan Brave Tickets: Students can receive tickets from any staff member when they are seen following the expectations throughout the building. The tickets will be turned into the office and Dr. Cannon will randomly draw tickets on Friday. If the student's ticket is drawn, they will come to the office to choose a prize!Bogan Brave Student of the Month: Our PBIS Committee selected character traits that we would like to focus on each month. At the end of each month, students in each class will nominate a classmate who has demonstrated this trait to be the Student of the Month. The Student of the Month will receive a certificate, have their photo taken, and will receive a Good News Call Home from Dr. Cannon.The expectations for the cafeteria, hallways, and restroom are below. It would be extremely helpful if you could also review these expectations at home!

summary:
Talawanda High School continues its **Positive Behavioral Interventions and Supports (PBIS)** program with exciting student recognition opportunities. Students can earn **Bogan Brave Tickets** from staff for following expectations, with weekly Friday prize drawings by Dr. Cannon. Monthly **Student of the Month** awards recognize students demonstrating specific character traits, earning certificates, photos, and Good News Calls home. 

**Cafeteria expectations** include: **Be Kind** (use appropriate language, say please/thank you, welcome everyone, help peers, listen to tablemates), **Be Safe** (enter/exit quietly with walking feet, stay seated, keep hands/feet to self, share food only from share table), and **Be Responsible** (use 3-inch voice, raise hand for help, follow adult directions, use tools appropriately, keep table and floor clean).

title: Student Attendance Policy and Chronic Absenteeism
source_title: Bogan Weekly News | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content: Attendance Reminders Student attendance is crucial to your student's success here at school.The state of Ohio defines chronic absenteeism as a student being absent for 10% of the year for both unexcused AND excused. In addition, the state looks at hours that a student has missed school- not just days. This mean that tardies in the morning and early dismissals in the afternoon contribute to chronic absenteeism.If your family has a fun trip planned, we absolutely encourage you to go and make those memories!! Please just be mindful of other days that your student is absent.We will send monthly letters home if your child has reached 10% or more absences. This is a way for us to proactively share information with you about your child's attendance.Please know that we are here to help!! Do not hesitate reach out if you have any questions or need assistance!

summary: **Attendance is essential for student success.** Ohio defines chronic absenteeism as missing 10% or more of the school year (excused or unexcused), calculated by hours missed—including tardies and early dismissals. Families will receive monthly letters if their student reaches 10% absence threshold. The school encourages families to take planned trips but asks them to be mindful of other absences, and offers help for any attendance concerns.

title: End of Year Message from Dr. Cannon
source_title: Bogan Weekly News | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content: A Message from Dr. Cannon Happy Friday!This final week was filled with celebration, reflection, and joy as students wrapped up learning, enjoyed end-of-year activities, and spent meaningful time with classmates and staff. We loved seeing their excitement as they celebrated a successful year of growth and achievement.Our students have made tremendous progress and should feel proud of their hard work and perseverance. From classroom learning to school events and performances, it has been a year full of growth and memorable experiences.It is such a privilege to be part of a school community that consistently comes together to support our students. This year has reflected what is possible when families, staff, and students work in partnership with shared purpose and care. Congratulations to our 5th graders and to the Talawanda Class of 2026! We wish you all the absolute best for your very bright futures. We hope you have an amazing summer!Sincerely,Dr. Kirsten Cannon, Principalps) I will be returning in the fall as Dr. Soros! 😁

summary: Dr. Cannon reflects on a successful final week filled with celebrations and end-of-year activities. Students showed tremendous growth throughout the year, and the school community came together to support their achievements. **Congratulations to 5th graders and the Talawanda Class of 2026!** Dr. Cannon will return in the fall as **Dr. Soros** after getting married.

source_title: Bogan Weekly News | Smore Newsletters for Education

Older Americans Month: Champion Your Health
Every May, Older Americans Month recognizes the contributions of older adults, highlights aging trends, and reaffirms commitments to serve our older community members. The 2026 theme is “Champion Your Health”.Throughout the month of May, Oxford Seniors, Age-Friendly Oxford, and the Coalition for a Healthy Community, Oxford Area are partnering to highlight and offer programming focused on promoting physical, mental, and emotional health and well-being at all ages.You can participate by playing “Community BINGO” with us! It’s as easy as 1, 2, 3!1) Print your own or pick up a Community Bingo card at any of the following locations:Oxford Seniors, 922 Tollgate Dr., OxfordOxford Lane Library, 441 S. Locust St.The Knolls of Oxford, Clubhouse or Front DeskScripps Gerontology Center, 396 Upham Hall, on campus2) Every time you do something listed on the card, mark it off. The goal is to get “BINGO” as many times as possible. A “BINGO” is marking off any 5 squares in a straight line – either vertically, horizontally, or diagonally.3) Bring your completed BINGO card to the Intergenerational BINGO Party on Sun. May 31 from 3:00 – 5:00 p.m. at Oxford Seniors for prizes, snacks, and FUN!

summary: Celebrate **Older Americans Month** in May by playing **Community BINGO**! Pick up a card at Oxford Seniors (922 Tollgate Dr.), Oxford Lane Library (441 S. Locust St.), The Knolls of Oxford, or Scripps Gerontology Center (396 Upham Hall). Complete activities like attending chair yoga, visiting parks, making art, attending concerts, and connecting with neighbors. Bring your completed card to the **Intergenerational BINGO Party on May 31, 3:00-5:00 PM** at Oxford Seniors for prizes and snacks.
